key_insight: An interpretable finite-element inverse framework identifies relative spatial variations in multiple hyperelastic constitutive parameters from displacement fields alone.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support characterization of graded composites and heterogeneous biological tissues without parameter-heavy deep-learning models.
method: Use full-field displacements to formulate the hyperelastic inverse problem.
Optimize parameter fields directly at the finite-element level.
evidence_signal: Validation on 3D synthetic and 2D experimental benchmarks covers heterogeneous, graded, and anisotropic hyperelastic materials, with acceptable accuracy and significantly lower computational time than recently reported deep-learning frameworks.
watch_item: The framework recovers relative parameter variation; absolute parameter calibration and robustness to measurement noise require further assessment.
paper_title: Interpretable identification of constitutive parameter field for three-dimensional heterogeneous and graded hyperelastic materials from full-field displacements
